name: One neutral picture of what the buyer was charged: list price, adjustments and per-line allocations
actor: Source adapter (system); read by documents, analytics, returns and the operator
trigger: An order is ingested or re-ingested from any channel that reports a reduction in any form
preconditions: The channel reports at least one of: a pre-reduction price, a reduction type, a reduction amount, a promotion id
Today none of these reach OrderItem: no list price, no line discount, no reason (r4/code/B-line-identity-traced.md section 3)
mainFlow: The adapter emits order-level adjustments {id, label, source, trigger, funder, form, qualifyingLineIds, allocationMethod}.
Per line it emits listUnitPriceGross (nullable = unknown), taxRate and allocations [{adjustmentId, amount | null}].
Core stores the facts unchanged as three-state fields (absent = not read, null/[] = source checked and has none).
Effective price paid stays the existing price / unitPriceGross; list minus allocations must reconcile to it or the line is flagged.
"Gift" and "bundle discount" are derived views over the facts, never stored tax classes.
altFlows: Allegro CAMPAIGN: originalPrice == price although a discount happened; listUnitPriceGross must be null (unknown), not equal to price.
Allegro ALLEGRO_PRICES: list = price + reconciliation.value, with an adjustment funder=channel (see X-07).
Several Allegro discount types on one line (array, no amounts): one adjustment per type, allocation amount null, total gap known only for the line.
Erli: one adjustment from order.rebate {id,name,code}; unitPriceBeforeRebate maps to list price ONLY when the rebate is the only reduction, else null.
Amazon v0: PromotionIds and PromotionDiscount live in different places; per-promotion amount is not recoverable with 2+ promotions on an item.
PrestaShop cart-rule gift merged into a paid row: no line-level fact exists; see D-03 and the gifts writer (G-03).

channelData.erli: items[].unitPrice, unitPriceBeforeRebate (integer, grosze likely), order.rebate {id, name, code}
channelData.prestashop: order_detail original_product_price, reduction_percent, reduction_amount (unread); order_cart_rules / total_discounts_tax_incl
channelData.shoper: order-products discount_perc on children (SDK only); parent discount field unknown
channelData.mirakl: order_lines.origin_unit_price, price_unit, promotions[] {id, deduced_amount, apportioned, configuration.type}
channelData.kaufland: order_unit.price (post-discount), discounts[] {usage_type voucher|volume, discount_value}, at most one per unit; Kaufland-funded promotions hidden

olBehaviour: New optional fields on IncomingOrderItem/OrderItem plus an order-level adjustments list; must be added in every allowlist in one change (ingestion builder, snapshot writer and reader, destination projection, invoice mapper, order_line_items writer, adapter pass-throughs). No capability: data only. Rendering on documents is a separate decision (D-04, G-10).

acceptance.given: an Allegro line with originalPrice 89.99, price 85.49 and discounts [{type: CAMPAIGN}]
acceptance.then: listUnitPriceGross is null and one adjustment with label CAMPAIGN and amount null is stored; nothing reports "no reduction"

acceptance.given: an Erli order with rebate {name: "Jesien"} and a line with unitPrice 9000, unitPriceBeforeRebate 10000
acceptance.then: one adjustment (source channel, funder unknown) and an allocation of 10.00 on that line are stored

acceptance.given: a channel that reports no reduction field at all
acceptance.then: the adjustments field is absent (not read), distinct from an empty list (checked, none)

acceptance.given: an operator discount applied through order edits (#3543)
acceptance.when: list and paid prices are compared
acceptance.then: the channel adjustment is read from the channel snapshot only, never derived as list minus the edited unitPriceGross

priorityReason: Differentiation, not pilot damage: r5/7 puts the neutral list price + reduction work in Stage 3 (G20), and no pilot document path needs it while documents keep the paid price.
evidence: verify/allegro-line-price.md Q1-Q4 (price and originalPrice are UNIT prices; LineItemDiscount type only; order-level discounts[] deprecated and absent from the current swagger)
risks: Evidence contradicts a naive model in three places: Allegro CAMPAIGN/ALLEGRO_PRICES (originalPrice is not a list price), Erli unitPriceBeforeRebate (not a list price, r5/3 C-023 point 3), and allocation amounts that are unknown per discount type. The proposed model survives only if listUnitPriceGross and allocation.amount are nullable.
Allowlist drift (C-055): three documented losses of an OrderItem field already.
Operator discount rewrites unitPriceGross (order-discount.types.ts:216-221, r5/6 N-3), so list minus paid mixes channel and OL reductions.
Allegro discount enum in practice differs from the spec (staff #9790 lists CROSSMULTIPACK, ALLEGRO_PRICES); unknown strings must parse as unknown, not error.

name: Per-piece channels: one order unit per piece is merged into lines with a quantity
trigger: A per-piece channel (Kaufland; also TikTok Shop and InPost Von Halsky per Apilo) sends an order with the same unit bought N times
preconditions: A source adapter for such a channel exists. OpenLinker has none today (libs/integrations list: no kaufland, amazon, mirakl, ebay)
mainFlow: The adapter groups order units by offer/unit id and price into one line with quantity N.
The adapter keeps the list of channel unit ids on the line (needed for per-unit returns and refunds).
A discount that differs between units of the same offer keeps those units on separate lines.
altFlows: Units of the same offer with different discount_value: separate lines, because merging would average the price.
A return or refund arrives per order unit: resolved to the merged line plus the unit id (see R-04).

channelData.kaufland: OrderUnit has no quantity field; "If the same unit gets ordered several times, several order units are created"; discounts[] at most one per unit; refund PATCH /order-units/{id}/refund {amount, reason}
channelData.apilo_reference: Per-integration setting "Strategia importu przedmiotow zamowienia": import singly / group by offer (TikTok Shop, InPost Von Halsky)

olBehaviour: Adapter-internal merge with the unit ids kept as data on the line; no core change. If ever needed, an operator setting per connection (import singly vs group), Apilo shape.

acceptance.given: a Kaufland order with 3 order units of the same unit at 19.99 and no discount
acceptance.then: one line with quantity 3 and the three unit ids is stored

acceptance.given: the same order where one unit carries a voucher discount
acceptance.then: two lines are stored (quantity 2 at full price, quantity 1 at the discounted price)

acceptance.given: a refund request for one of three merged units
acceptance.when: OpenLinker sends it to the channel
acceptance.then: it addresses that unit id, not the merged line

priorityReason: No Kaufland (or other per-piece) adapter exists in the repository, so there is nothing to merge for the pilot or any current user.
risks: Kaufland hides Kaufland-funded promotions, so the merged line price can understate the list price with no signal (see X-07).
Merging loses unit ids unless they are kept; per-piece returns would then be unmatched.

name: Per-connection settings and adapter declarations for how a channel encodes bundles, gifts and discounts
trigger: A connection is set up, or a channel shape is found that the adapter cannot tell apart on its own (for example parent + children lines)
preconditions: The behaviour differs per plugin or shop setup, not per platform (WooCommerce bundle plugins, Shoper sets, PrestaShop pack stock modes)
mainFlow: The adapter declares only facts about its own platform or device limits (for example per-line rebate support, zero-line acceptance), as a required method on the document ports where all adapters are ours (ADR-046 shape).
Choices that change document content or stock behaviour are operator settings on the connection (ADR-082 shape: default plus overrides).
Examples of settings: "this source emits bundle children as lines" (suppress or keep), "show free items on documents: omit | show", "bundle on documents: one line | components".
The settings page shows the effective value and where it came from (declared, default, operator).
altFlows: Declaration absent (older or out-of-tree adapter): conservative default, shown as "not declared" in the UI, never silently treated as supported.
A setting would contradict a declaration (operator picks "show free items" on a printer that refuses zero lines): refused at save with the reason.

channelData.woocommerce: Product Bundles: _bundled_by, _bundled_items, _bundled_item_priced_individually in line meta_data (unread today)
channelData.shoper: order-products type 1 + children[] (SDK only; unread today, C-019)
channelData.prestashop: pack_stock_type per product, read path differs by version (C-014)
channelData.competitors: Linnworks connector flags (CanCancelOrderLines, IsRefundsVisible); Apilo per-integration import strategy; Sellasist per-integration "Sposob naliczania rabatow"; BaseLinker per-connector advanced settings

olBehaviour: Settings live in Connection.config (no migration), read through pure readers like readStockSafetyBuffer; declarations are required methods on InvoicingPort/FiscalizationPort only for device limits. ADR-082 is the precedent: adapter declares ReceiptLineNameBudget, operator chooses delivery rendering.

acceptance.given: a WooCommerce connection with "children emitted as lines" set to suppress
acceptance.when: an order with a bundle container and two children arrives
acceptance.then: only the container is reserved and picked; children are kept for display

acceptance.given: a document adapter with no declaration method (out-of-tree plugin)
acceptance.when: the operator opens the document settings
acceptance.then: the page says "not declared" and the conservative rule (no zero lines, no line rebates) applies

acceptance.given: an eparagony connection that declares zero lines refused
acceptance.when: the operator sets free items to "show"
acceptance.then: the save is refused with the device reason

priorityReason: r5/7 defers all declarers and channel-shape ingestion; the pilot needs only a guard refusing a bundle definition on a WooCommerce container, which belongs to the bundles writer.
evidence: r5/6-design-and-code.md section 3 items 3, 6, 7 and section 4 (ADR-046, ADR-082)
r5/7-scope-overengineering.md section 5 (declarers deferred) and section 9 item 5
risks: Each guard-only declaration needs a server read and a frontend mirror (ADR-046 amendment), so the "2-4 declarations" cost is understated (r5/6).
ADR-048 decision 1 forbids an interface with no implementer; ship a declaration only with its first adapter.

name: A line added after the order exists (shop back-office edit, operator edit in OpenLinker)
actor: Shop staff (source edit); operator (OpenLinker edit); gift rule (automation)
trigger: A re-ingested order carries a line it did not have, or an operator or rule wants to add a gift or bundle line
preconditions: The order was already ingested and may already be reserved, routed or invoiced
mainFlow: Source edit: the amendment diff reports line-added (order-amendment-diff.ts:52, :163); the new line goes through item resolution, reservation and, if routed, re-routing like a new line.
If a document was already issued, the added line needs its own correction or a second document; never a silent rewrite of the issued document.
OpenLinker edit: an add-line edit writes into the orderEdits overlay (never into the channel snapshot, #3542), with the same refusal rules and lock as other edits.
An added line carries its origin (channel, operator, rule) so writebacks know whether the channel knows it (see X-09).
altFlows: PrestaShop back office adds a product and a cart rule adds a gift as a side effect (AddProductToOrderHandler.php:261-262); gift detection must run on updates, not only first ingestion.
Order already shipped: the added line cannot be packed with the original parcel; it is held for operator decision.
Order was once awaiting_mapping: order.received never fires again, so a rule-added gift never runs (r5/6 N-1).

channelData.prestashop: Back-office AddProductToOrderHandler: updates an existing row (quantity += delta) or creates a new one via createList
channelData.allegro: No seller-side line add after purchase (no evidence of one)
channelData.shoper: Back-office edits sync per Apilo (S12); not verified for OpenLinker

olBehaviour: Core change: today edits can only lower quantities (order-edits.types.ts:76, :288) and the edit write path lives in apps/api (order-edit.service.ts:181, :532), so a worker-side rule cannot call it. An add-line edit needs a core writer with lock and refusal rules.

acceptance.given: a routed order re-ingested with a new line
acceptance.then: an amendment line-added is recorded and the new line is reserved; existing lines keep their holds

acceptance.given: an invoiced order that gains a line at source
acceptance.then: the issued invoice is unchanged and the order shows "added after invoicing" for operator action

acceptance.given: an order that went through awaiting_mapping before becoming ready
acceptance.then: the order.received trigger fires once (fixing N-1) or the gap is shown

priorityReason: On the pilot stack Allegro orders cannot gain lines and own-shop orders are not routed (#3487 skip), and r5/7 sizes operator add-line alone as an L in Stage 3.
risks: What reservation and routing do today with a line added on re-ingestion of a routed order was not traced (unverified).
Sellasist explicitly does not re-sync shop edits; doing it here creates amendments the operator must understand.

name: Lines that are neither goods nor a discount: deposit, store credit, wallet, points, packaging, paid services
trigger: An order carries a deposit, a points or store-credit payment, a packaging line or a paid additional service
preconditions: The channel reports the item in a field OpenLinker does not map today, or as an ordinary line
mainFlow: The adapter classifies the item: goods line, service line (gift wrap, see D-05), deposit, or payment instrument.
A voucher, gift card, points or wallet payment is a payment, not an adjustment: the goods line keeps its full price (EU Art. 30a).
A deposit is carried per line as its own amount and VAT treatment, never folded into the goods price.
Service and deposit lines are excluded from picking and stock but kept on documents per the document policy.
altFlows: Allegro deposit on a product set: one summed deposit per line; a component return then needs a split the order does not give (hold for operator).
IdoSell orderSalesMode points or money: the line is paid with points (redemption), not discounted.
Packaging line at 0.00 (BaseLinker shows packaging like gifts): classified as non-stock, never as a gift.

channelData.allegro: lineItems[].deposit (LineItemDeposit: sum of component deposits), vouchers, selectedAdditionalServices[] {definitionId, name, price, quantity}; RefundDetails.deposits[], additionalServices (one amount per order)
channelData.ebay: giftDetails = digital gift card line items only

olBehaviour: Field: a neutral line kind or separate order-level lists for deposits, services and payment instruments; each kind reaches documents through the same allowlists as X-01.

acceptance.given: an Allegro product-set line with a deposit of 1.50
acceptance.then: the deposit is stored apart from the line price and appears on the document per the document policy

acceptance.given: an order paid partly with a gift card
acceptance.then: the goods lines keep full price and the gift card is a payment form, not a rebate

acceptance.given: a 0.00 packaging line
acceptance.when: the order reaches the pack bench
acceptance.then: it is not shown as a gift and is not counted as stock

priorityReason: No evidence ties deposits or points to the pilot client, and the one money loss in this family (paid gift wrap) is split out as D-05.
risks: Whether Allegro vouchers reduce price or pay part of it was not checked (unverified).
Deposit VAT treatment per country not researched.

name: Adjustment audit trail per line: who or what applied it, before and after values
trigger: Someone asks why a line has the price it has (buyer complaint, refund dispute, tax check)
preconditions: Adjustments come from three sources: channel (X-01), operator edits (#3543 order.discount_change), rules (gift automation)
mainFlow: Every adjustment stores source, actor (user id, rule id or channel), time and the line values before and after.
Channel adjustments are facts as received and are re-recorded only when a re-ingestion changes them (amendment).
Operator discounts already land in order_changes with history; rule-applied adjustments use the automation run record.
The order detail shows one timeline per line combining the three.
altFlows: A re-ingestion changes a channel adjustment after a document was issued: the timeline shows both values and the document keeps the old one.

channelData.competitors: BaseLinker discount log value_before, value_after, details, profile_id (-1 = API), date_add; Sellasist action logs without per-line values; Apilo change history without values

olBehaviour: Mostly existing records (order_changes for operator edits, automation_runs for rules); new only for channel adjustments, which can live on the X-01 adjustment rows with received-at.

acceptance.given: an operator discount of 10.00 on an order
acceptance.when: the operator opens the line history
acceptance.then: it shows the user, time, 0.00 before and 10.00 after

acceptance.given: a channel adjustment that changes on re-ingestion
acceptance.then: both values and their times are shown

priorityReason: Depends on X-01 data that is itself deferred; operator discounts already have an audit record today.
risks: No merchant-voice evidence that operators ask for this; demand is inferred from competitors (BaseLinker has it "Full").

name: Who funded a reduction: seller, channel or unknown
actor: Source adapter; margin and gift-cost reports; document policy
trigger: A line is cheaper than the seller's price because the platform paid part of it (Allegro Prices, Kaufland-funded promotion, Erli rebate)
preconditions: The channel exposes the platform-funded part somewhere other than the line price, or hides it
mainFlow: The adapter sets adjustment.funder: seller, channel, other or unknown.
Allegro: reconciliation.value x quantity is a channel-funded amount; the line list price is price + reconciliation.value.
Erli: funder unknown on the order since donorType was removed (2026-08-19); resolvable only from billing rebateOrigin.
Kaufland: funder seller for discounts[]; channel-funded promotions are not on the order at all.
Reports and any document rule read funder; a document policy holds rather than guesses when funder is unknown and the answer would change the tax base.
altFlows: Funder unknown and the tax question unresolved: documents use the price the buyer paid (today's behaviour) and the order is flagged for the adviser question, not blocked.

channelData.allegro: reconciliation {value, type BILLING|WALLET, quantity}; discounts[].type ALLEGRO_PRICES (staff #9790)
channelData.kaufland: "Only seller-created discounts appear here. Kaufland-funded promotions are not reflected in this field."

olBehaviour: Field on the X-01 adjustment; no capability. Margin (ADR-080) and gift-cost reports read it.

acceptance.given: an Allegro line at 59.99 with reconciliation.value 7.97
acceptance.then: listUnitPriceGross is 67.96 and an adjustment of 7.97 with funder channel is stored

acceptance.given: an Erli order with a rebate
acceptance.then: the adjustment has funder unknown

priorityReason: The only consequence that could rank it higher, a different VAT base under EU Art. 73, is unverified for these platforms and waits for the tax adviser.
evidence: verify/allegro-line-price.md Q4 (Allegro Ceny: originalPrice == price == reduced price; seller price = price + reconciliation.value, per item x reconciliation.quantity; CAMPAIGN/COUPON folded into price, funder not documented)
r5/1-allegro-pl.md C-003 row and section 2 item 5
r5/3-marketplaces-countries.md C-023 point 4 and section 3 A1
risks: Whether a platform subsidy enters the seller's VAT base is a tax-adviser question (Art. 73 reading by r5/3, not a ruling).
The proposed adjustment model needs funder on the adjustment, not on the line; Allegro reconciliation is per line, which fits as one channel adjustment per line.

preconditions: Some line has origin operator or rule, or is a derived component id like {lineId}~c:{variantId}
mainFlow: Every writeback that names channel line ids filters to lines whose origin is the channel.
A derived component id is mapped back to its channel line id before any writeback.
A refund for an OpenLinker-only line is recorded in OpenLinker only (no channel line to refund).
altFlows: All lines of a parcel are OpenLinker-only: the waybill is relayed for the order without line ids (Allegro allows an empty list meaning every item).

channelData.allegro: CheckoutFormAddWaybillRequest lineItems[]{id} only; empty list = every item; RefundLineItem by lineItem.id

acceptance.then: only the channel line id is sent

acceptance.given: a component line {L}~c:{v}
acceptance.then: the waybill names L

name: Operator quantity edit or cancel of a bundle line is refused until edits understand components
trigger: An operator lowers the quantity of, or cancels part of, an order line that has a bundle expansion
preconditions: Stage 1 bundles: reservations, work lines and decrements carry component ids {lineId}~c:{variantId} while edits address the bundle line id
mainFlow: The edit service checks the frozen expansion; a bundle line edit is refused with a named code (for example LINE_IS_BUNDLE) and nothing is written.
Later, one "bundle line id -> frozen component lines" read feeds the four follow-ups and aggregates results back to the bundle line for the response.
altFlows: Whole-order cancel: unaffected, because reverseForOrder and hold release are row-based.

channelData.any: Not channel data; all channels whose lines are bundles in OpenLinker

Without it four follow-ups silently miss: assessForEdit (QUANTITY_BELOW_FULFILLED never fires), lowerLineQuantity (returns unrouted, cancels no units), narrowForOrder (holds not lowered), reverseLineQuantity (no stock given back).

acceptance.then: the edit is refused with LINE_IS_BUNDLE and holds, works and stock are unchanged

The bundles writer may also list this guard; it is here because order edits are a cross-cutting path.
Every miss is a silent no-op, so tests must assert effects, not just "no error".

name: Bundle on the receipt or invoice: one line or components, and mixed-VAT price split
actor: Document composer (system); operator choosing the policy; tax adviser
trigger: An order with a recognised bundle line is invoiced or fiscalised
preconditions: The bundle line resolves to an OpenLinker bundle definition (bundles writer, B-01/B-04)
Decision D3 (2026-09-28): the order line and documents keep the bundle
mainFlow: Default (pilot): the document carries the bundle as one line at the price paid and the bundle's own rate (D3). PrestaShop packs already arrive like this: one row at the pack's own rate whatever the components' rates (verify/prestashop-live.md).
At definition time a warning is shown when component rates differ from the bundle's rate (pilot guard, Stage 1).
Later, an operator setting per connection chooses one line vs component lines.

Component prices are computed at sale time, proportional to each component's standalone gross selling price x quantity (design B), split exactly to the minor unit with the remainder on the largest part, and frozen on the order for documents and refunds.
An operator override with per-component in-set prices (design A) is allowed only with a recorded reason, shares that sum to the bundle price, and no component above its standalone price.
altFlows: Component with no standalone price: fall back to cost (MF 2017 notice allows purchase or production cost); if no cost either, hold the document with a named reason, never an equal split.
Bundle priced ABOVE the sum of standalone prices: proportional split breaches the BFH test for every component; hold for operator and adviser (no source covers it).
Single composite supply (phone with charger): one rate is correct even with separate prices shown (C-41/04 Levob, C-463/16, KIS 2026 S.IG); "components when rates differ" must not be a core default.
Fiscal printer: a bundle name whose rate changes with composition can lock the name (ADR-082 context); component names or a stable rate per name are required.

channelData.allegro: one lineItems[].tax.rate per line even for a product set
channelData.shopify_reference: discount allocated to components by weighted price; tax per component
channelData.competitors: Apilo proportional to "Cena brutto w zestawie", no cap; Brightpearl and Linnworks parent carries price, children 0 (Linnworks equal split on customs labels); Sellasist chooses by split timing

olBehaviour: Pilot: nothing new on documents (D3). Later: operator setting (one line | components), a pure split function in sales-documents, and the in-set price data from the bundles work. Choosing a tax treatment in core would breach ADR-063.

acceptance.given: a bundle defined with components at 5% and 23% and a bundle rate of 23%
acceptance.then: a warning says documents will show one line at 23%

acceptance.given: the component-lines setting, a bundle paid 100.00 and standalone prices 70.00 and 50.00 at sale time
acceptance.then: component lines are 58.33 and 41.67, each at its own rate, and the split is stored on the order

acceptance.given: an operator override giving the 5% component 90.00 of a 100.00 bundle whose standalone price is 50.00
acceptance.then: it is refused: share above standalone price

acceptance.given: the component-lines setting and a component with no standalone price and no cost
acceptance.then: it is held with reason "bundle split key missing"

priorityReason: D3 decided documents keep the bundle line; splitting reverses it and needs the tax adviser (r5/7 sections 1 and 5, D3a/D3c deferred).
evidence: verify/bundle-price-split.md sections 1-4 (MF notice 29.09.2017 primary; CJEU C-349/96 CPP, Madgett and Baldwin; BFH XI R 19/23 Leitsatz and Rn 7, 13; design B default, A as override)
r5/8-tax-fiscal.md C-035 (XI R 22/22 rejected capping as a method)
risks: Mixed-VAT kits documented as one line may be over- or under-taxed during the pilot (seller money, legal question).
MF 2017 warns a disproportionate split can be treated as abuse of law; KIS accepted non-proportional splits only with an economic reason on record (secondary summaries, not full text).
The BFH cap is an exclusion test and capping is not itself an accepted method (XI R 22/22): show it as a warning or refusal, never as an allocation algorithm.
Claim that Apilo and Sellasist use typed in-set prices was not re-verified against primary docs (verify/bundle-price-split.md section 4).

name: Free item on the receipt or invoice: allocated price, 1 grosz, internal record, or zero line
actor: Document composer (system); operator choosing the policy; tax adviser
trigger: An order with a line whose value is fully covered by adjustments (derived gift view, X-01) is invoiced or fiscalised
preconditions: The free line is known as such (channel flag, 0.00 line, or OpenLinker-added); gift recognition is the gifts writer's scope (G-01..G-05)
mainFlow: Per connection the operator records the gift treatment (neutral names): priced-in | symbolic | gratuitous | zero-line, and who chose it (ADR-082 shape).

priced-in (default candidate): the paid total is allocated proportionally by list price over paid lines and the gift, never above the gift's own list price; every line is an ordinary positive line at its own rate.
symbolic: the gift is a 1 grosz line at its own rate; the paid total is carried by the other lines.
gratuitous: the gift is omitted from the buyer document and an internal record is made (D-07); art. 7 ust. 2 supplies are exempt from the cash register and not invoiced.
zero-line (0.00 or list price + 100% line rebate): offered only after an adviser sign-off, because KIS 2026 classes exactly this shape as a gratuitous supply.
The adapter declares device limits only (D-04): positive bucket required, per-line rebate supported.
altFlows: Gift at a different VAT rate than the paid lines and treatment is omit or move-value: refused with a named reason (both shift tax between rates; the higher-rate-gift direction under-declares).
Gift at the same rate as the paid lines: omitting it from the document is tax-neutral and allowed (KIS 2015 ILPP1/4512-1-199/15).
Treatment unset or adapter undeclared: the gift is recorded on the order and the document is held when rates differ, omitted when they match; never a silent fold.
Allocation rounding would leave the gift's rate bucket at 0.00: move the remainder so the bucket stays positive or hold (D-02).

The proposed neutral model has no field for the treatment; it must be an operator setting plus an order-level record of what was applied, not a property of the adjustment.

name: A rounding or delivery remainder lands on a free line and turns a gift into a paid 0.01

preconditions: reconcileDiscountRounding runs (discountTotal > 0 and a positive gap) or spreadDeliveryAcrossLines runs in spread mode
mainFlow: The allocators skip lines whose paid gross is 0 when choosing where a remainder goes.
If every quantity-1 line is free, the remainder goes to the largest paid line, splitting it if needed (existing rule).
The fix keeps the zero-bucket guard in mind: a free line left at 0.00 may then trigger D-02 on eparagony and must be handled there, not by keeping the cent.
altFlows: No paid line can take the remainder (all lines free): the document is held with a named reason.

name: Refuse a zero-value VAT bucket before calling eparagony, with an operator-facing cause
actor: Fiscalization composer and eparagony adapter (system); operator
trigger: A receipt would contain a VAT letter whose net value after line rebates and REBATE lines is 0.00 or below
preconditions: eparagony refuses such a receipt with HTTP 400 errorCode 41 "Incorrectly calculated value of eReceipt.lines[n]" before the printer
mainFlow: Before the call, the adapter sums each VAT letter after line rebates and REBATE lines.
If any letter would be 0.00 or below, the receipt is not sent; the registration is held with a cause naming the line and rate ("free item alone in its VAT rate").
The operator can change the gift treatment (G-10), remove the line, fix the rate in the master, or issue manually.
A whole-receipt REBATE without a rate is sent only when the operator chose proportional allocation; otherwise discounts go as REBATE lines with the taxRate of the line they reduce.
altFlows: eparagony still returns error 41 for another reason: the raw message is mapped to the same operator cause with the vendor text attached.
A rate left at 0.01 is accepted but overstates the receipt total by 0.01; not used as a workaround.

trigger: An order whose lines sum to more than its total (PrestaShop cart rule, coupon, merged cart-rule gift row) is invoiced or fiscalised
preconditions: assertLinesSumToTotal refuses a gap above a quantity-scaled epsilon (invoice mapper :304-340, fiscal mapper :214-255); the refusal names the discount cause (#3365)
mainFlow: Today: the document is held with a cause naming the discount.
Later: an operator setting per connection allows proportional allocation of an order-level discount across goods lines (MF communique as quoted in KIS 703725), exact to the minor unit.
With allocation on, each line carries list price and rebate (X-01) so KSeF P_10 or eparagony REBATE with taxRate can render it.
Allocation never touches a 0.00 line and never zeroes a VAT letter on a receipt (D-01, D-02).

Discount equal to or above the goods total: refused (distributeOrderDiscount returns null), document held.

name: Return of one bundle component: refund including the lost bundle discount, restock that component
actor: Buyer (returns); operator (receives, decides refund); system (restock, credit note)
trigger: A buyer returns part of a bundle bought as one line
preconditions: The order line is a bundle with a frozen expansion (bundles writer, B-10)
The channel reports the return at bundle grain (Allegro offerId + quantity)
mainFlow: The return line resolves to the bundle order line (by offerId / SKU, #3171).
At receipt the operator says which components came back and in what quantity.
Restock targets those component variants in the master that owns them, using the frozen expansion; today return-custody.service.ts:931-940 restocks the bundle variant instead.

The default refund and credit value of a returned component is the value attributed to it on the original document, frozen at sale (art. 29a ust. 10 pkt 2 "wartosc zwroconych towarow"), never recomputed from current catalogue prices.

Clawing back the lost bundle discount is an operator option (commercial term of the offer): the refund is lowered and the reason recorded; whether the kept component's document line is also corrected is an adviser question.
altFlows: No frozen component split (pilot-period order, documents kept the bundle line): manual refund, restock and credit (R-01, R-05).
All components returned: an ordinary full return of the bundle line.
Allegro refund for one component: only RefundLineItem type AMOUNT on the bundle lineItem is possible.
One Fulfillment (Allegro warehouse) return: FulfillmentRefundDisposition.product carries gtins and quantity per product.

name: Partial return from a discounted flexible bundle or multibuy: claw back the lost discount
trigger: A buyer returns some lines of an Allegro flexible bundle (N lines with BUNDLE) or some units of a multibuy
preconditions: Each bundle member is its own lineItem with a proportionally reduced price (flexible bundle) or the units share one discounted line (multibuy)
mainFlow: OpenLinker groups the lines carrying the same channel bundle evidence (X-01 adjustment with the same id or BUNDLE type).
On a partial return it proposes refund = paid price of returned items minus the lost discount on kept items, when the operator chooses the claw-back rule.
The proposal states both figures; the operator confirms; the ceiling (#3289) still applies.

name: Allegro duplicate identical lines: same offer twice, one in a bundle, return cannot pick the line
trigger: An Allegro order has two lineItems with the same offer and price, one with discounts [BUNDLE] and one with discounts null, and the buyer returns one unit
preconditions: Allegro returns carry offerId and quantity only; Allegro staff declined to add a line id
mainFlow: Resolution narrows by offerId then unit price; two survivors remain, so the result is ambiguous and resolvedOrderLineId stays null.
Because both lines have the same price, OpenLinker picks the line by a stated rule (the line not carrying BUNDLE first) only when the money is identical, and records that it chose.
When prices differ, price breaks the tie (flexible bundle with a real discount).
altFlows: Prices identical and BUNDLE present on both: stays ambiguous; restock is unaffected (same product) and the credit uses the shared price.

name: Freeze each bundle component's allocated price at sale so later credits use the documented value
actor: System (expansion snapshot); operator later issuing the credit
trigger: A bundle order is ingested during the pilot (documents keep the bundle line, no in-set prices)
preconditions: Stage 1 bundle expansion is written once per order (insert-if-absent)
mainFlow: When the expansion row is written, it also stores each component's standalone gross price at that moment and the resulting proportional share of the paid bundle price (or null when unknown).
Later component returns and credits (B-15) use the frozen share: the value attributed at sale is what a correction must lower (art. 29a ust. 10 pkt 2).
Orders without frozen values fall back to manual valuation.
altFlows: Component has no catalogue price at ingestion: stored as null; that order's component credit is manual.

name: Restock of a returned PrestaShop pack writes a stock row PrestaShop ignores
trigger: A returned item whose product is a PrestaShop pack with stock from components (pack_stock_type 1, or 0 read as shop default) is restocked
preconditions: The pack product is mastered by PrestaShop with pack_stock_type 1 (decrement products only), or 3 resolving to 1, and the operator disposes the return as restock
mainFlow: PrestaShop adjustInventory detects a components-mode pack (readPackDefinition + resolvePackStockMode, already used in listInventory).
It refuses before writing with a typed NotSupported-style error; the restock is recorded as blocked with "pack stock comes from components: restock components".
The operator restocks components by manual correction (#3566).
altFlows: Pack in pack-only mode (0 on 9.2.0+, explicit): the write is correct and proceeds.
Later: the adapter restocks components itself like PrestaShop's own flow (M, needs per-component idempotency).
